points: A rubber duck is a duck-shaped toy, usually yellow with a flat base, made of rubber or rubber-like material such as vinyl.
Rubber ducks were invented in the late 19th century, when rubber became easier to shape.
The yellow rubber duck has become an iconic figure in Western pop culture and is often symbolically linked to bathing.
The earliest rubber ducks were made of harder vulcanized rubber, which made them unable to float, so they were intended as chew toys.
In 1948, Hong Kong company Winsome Plastic Works began producing rubber duck toys designed by its founder L.T. Lam.
A toy duck design patent was filed December 29, 1947 and granted April 26, 1949.
The design was later reproduced as a floating toy, with over 50 million sold.
Novelty rubber duck variations include character ducks for professions, politicians, or celebrities, introduced by Mark Boldt's Rubba Ducks.
In 2001, The Sun reported Queen Elizabeth II had a rubber duck wearing an inflatable crown in her bathroom, spotted by a workman.
The story briefly raised UK rubber duck sales by 80%.
The 2011 Guinness record for largest rubber duck collection was 5,631 ducks, awarded to Charlotte Lee.
In 2013 the rubber duck was inducted into the Toy Hall of Fame in Rochester, New York, alongside the game of chess.
Toys are selected for the Toy Hall of Fame based on factors like icon-status, longevity, and innovation.
Ernie from Sesame Street has performed the song "Rubber Duckie" multiple times and frequently spoke to and carried his rubber duckie.
C. W. McCall's song "Convoy" and its movie and novel are narrated by a character using the handle "Rubber Duck" and a bathtub toy on his Mack truck.
The Akron RubberDucks, formerly the Aeros, adopted the nickname on October 29, 2013, honoring Akron's rubber industry history.
Rubber ducks became a protest symbol in Belgrade, Brazil, and Moscow in 2017, and in Bangkok in 2020.
Dutch artist Florentijn Hofman created the world's largest rubber duck in 2007, about 600 kilograms in weight.
Hofman's ducks of various sizes have been displayed in many cities across several countries since 2007.
In 2013, China's Great Firewall blocked searches for "big yellow duck" after activists photoshopped the Rubber Duck into the Tank Man photo.
When the term "Big Yellow Duck" was searched, a message said search results could not be shown under relevant laws and policies.
Rubber duck races, also called derby duck races, are a fundraising method used by organizations worldwide.
People donate by sponsoring a duck; at the drive's end, ducks are dumped into a waterway and the first past the finish line wins a prize for its sponsor.
In the United States, rubber ducks are associated with the Jeep brand of sport utility vehicles.
Some Jeep owners custom-leave a rubber duck on another Jeep's hood as a compliment or random act of kindness.
In January 1992, a Pacific storm washed 28,800 Friendly Floatees bath toys off a ship; two-thirds floated south and reached Indonesia, Australia, and South America three months later.
The remaining 10,000 toys drifted north to Alaska, then completed a circle back near Japan, carried by the North Pacific Gyre.
Many toys entered the Bering Strait, were trapped in Arctic ice, and moved about one mile (1.6 km) per day.
The toys were sighted in the North Atlantic in 2000.
American oceanographer Curtis Ebbesmeyer monitored the movement of the toys.
Sun and seawater bleached the ducks and beavers white, while the turtles and frogs kept their original colors.
The incident inspired Donovan Hohn's 2011 book Moby-Duck and Eric Carle's 2005 picture book 10 Little Rubber Ducks.
A football-sized probe with GPS, pressure sensor, thermometer and accelerometer was lowered by rope into one of the glacier's moulins.
The probe was designed to find structures such as waterfalls inside the ice.
The probe went silent, so researchers also put ninety rubber ducks into the moulins.
The ducks were marked in English, Danish, and Inuit with 'science experiment' and 'reward' text plus an email address for finders.
As of 2012, none of the ducks had been found or returned, possibly because they were trapped in large aquifers inside the ice.

summary.overview: This summary covers the rubber duck's origins and design, its cultural roles, fundraising and brand uses, and its use in ocean drift and glacier research.
